# Cross-course coordination of fixed support budgets

A separate allocation per course maximizes the smaller predicted group recall in each course. The prior study scores the smaller recall pooled across courses. Test whether optimizing the pooled criterion directly changes who is reviewed and improves realized outcomes at fixed capacity. Each course retains its own seats and FA*IR prefix requirements. Recorded female/male fields define the two analysis groups. Within each group score order is fixed. Historical outcomes are observational, and budgets are hypothetical.

Compare unrestricted, adjusted FA*IR, quota, discounted ranking, local point-score thresholds and robust local thresholds from the original allocation engine. Add an exact pooled objective with each course's existing 0.01-per-seat score-utility constraint. The primary candidate uses the same objective with a shared utility slack of 0.01 times total seats relative to the maximum prefix-feasible score sum. This allows utility to move across courses without moving seats. Include a greedy one-seat-at-a-time pooled optimizer with the same global slack as a comparator. Both exact methods maximize minimum pooled predicted recall, then maximize pooled expected captures within 1e-8 normalized recall of the optimum. Preserve all ties and losses. Record objective values, prefix validity, seats, membership changes and predicted versus realized utility.

Use two existing, previously studied public archives for a new retrospective comparison. In OULAD use the 2013B and 2013J learners and existing eligibility filters from the prior transport study. Fit on all available 2013B learners and score all eligible 2013J courses with at least ten learners and both recorded groups. In UCI 697 use every row with a recorded Dropout/Graduate/Enrolled label. Split 60/40 by SHA-256 of the decimal zero-based source row number modulo ten, first six buckets for training. Use course, gender, previous qualification and application mode as categorical variables, age at enrollment, admission grade and previous qualification grade as numeric. Target recorded dropout; keep enrolled in the comparison population. Same course eligibility filter. Registration and admission scores are proxies for day-zero risk. One fixed registration per learner in OULAD, independent rows assumed in UCI without released identifiers. Fit the archived logistic model and 40 training-bootstrap variants separately at each institution. Do not tune on the scored data. Break score ties by the lexical row key. Record archive checksums. No independent institution is held in reserve for this jointly reported screen.

Keep floor(10% of eligible learners) seats per course. Fit and choose every policy before joining the evaluation outcomes to its decisions. Compare realized worst-group recall with every constrained comparator. A strong development result requires a gain of at least two percentage points and a positive paired lower bound against each on both cohorts, and a precision lower bound of at least −.01 versus unrestricted ranking on both. Use 5,000 within-course paired learner bootstrap replicates, seed 1701, conditional on fixed decisions. Report marginal percentile intervals and undefined draws. Overlapping pools, retrospective reuse and uncertainty in fitted risks limit generalization. A tied rank list only supports finite-cohort equality.
